conditions.host: macOS on Apple Silicon, Docker Desktop, linux/arm64 containers, ports bound to 127.0.0.1
conditions.install: every repeat is a fresh install on an empty PostgreSQL database; no in-place upgrade was run
conditions.time_zone: container defaults (UTC); the case holds no time value
conditions.acting_role: neteng, a non-superuser created by the superuser through the REST API, with object permissions view/add/change on ipam.vlangroup, and its own API token
conditions.gate_B_and_C: the same to-version instance serves B (group campus-a) and C (group campus-c)
conditions.parallelism: from-version and to-version stacks ran side by side on two ports; they share nothing

database_outcome.read_via: PostgreSQL in the database container; GET /api/ipam/vlan-groups/{id}/ as a second witness

sealed.prediction_detail: The POST answers 201. The group is created with the default range 1..4094 instead of 100..199, so a VLAN with ID 500 can then be added to it.

requests_as_run.old_workflow: POST /api/ipam/vlan-groups/ with {"name": "campus-a", "slug": "campus-a", "min_vid": 100, "max_vid": 199}, header Authorization: Token <redacted>; HTTP 201 is success
requests_as_run.stored_value_read: ipam_vlangroup row of the returned id, with psql inside the PostgreSQL container

disposition_rule: protocol README table, applied mechanically to the stored values below; the VLAN probes are supplementary and do not enter the rule
notes: Gate C uses a second group (campus-c) on the instance that served gate B; the request is otherwise the sealed correct path.
After each stored value was read, the superuser tried to add VLAN 500 and VLAN 150 to the group, to show what the stored range means for the business outcome.

Business outcome, from the supplementary probes: on v4.0.11 the group refused VLAN 500 (400, 'VID must be between 100 and 199') in 3 of 3 repeats; on v4.1.0 the group made by the old workflow accepted VLAN 500 (201) in 3 of 3; the group made by the correct path refused it (400, 'VID must be in ranges 100-199') in 3 of 3. VLAN 150 was accepted everywhere.

The 201 body of the write on v4.1.0 does carry vid_ranges, so a client that inspects the response could see the miss. That body is also off by one against the database and against a later read: it shows [[1,4093]] where the row holds {"[1,4095)"} and a GET shows [[1,4094]], and [[100,198]] where the row holds {"[100,200)"} and a GET shows [[100,199]]. The stored value in this file is always the database row.
The stored default range on v4.1.0 is the one the sealed list predicted: {"[1,4095)"}.
No hold overlapped any observation, and no repeat was voided or repeated. The lane's containers together stayed under 1 GiB.
